Then $t(s^k(a - b, b))$, the daughter of the $k$-fold son of $(a - b, b)$, has first entry $(k+1)a - kb$ and second entry $ka - (k-1)b$, and $s(t^k(c, d - c))$, the son of the $k$-fold…
nodes.title: Levels of the branches of an arch

nodes.summary: As lists of numerator–denominator pairs, row $1$ of the Calkin–Wilf tree is $(1, 2), (2, 1)$ and row $2$ is $(1, 3), (3, 2), (2, 3), (3, 1)$, in this order.
nodes.title: The first rows of the Calkin–Wilf tree

nodes.summary: Row $k$ of the Calkin–Wilf tree is a list of numerator–denominator pairs, the pair $(a, b)$ standing for $a/b$. Row $0$ is the single pair $(1, 1)$, and row $k + 1$ is obtained from row $k$ by replacing each pair $(a, b)$, in order, by its two children $(a, a + b)$ and $(a + b, b)$.
nodes.title: Rows of the Calkin–Wilf tree

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $a_0, \dots, a_r$ write $[a_0, \dots, a_r]$ for the continued fraction $a_0 + 1/(a_1 + 1/(\cdots + 1/a_r))$, and $1^j$ for a block of $j$ ones; read a positive rational $u/v$ in lowest terms as the position $(u, v)$ of the Euclid game. nodes.title: Continued fractions with maximal optimal play in Euclid

nodes.summary: For $k \ge 2$ let $T_k$ be the number of vertices of row $k$ of the Calkin–Wilf tree of the form $(2m+n)/(m+n)$ with $m/n$ a P-position of Euclid in row $k - 2$. Then $3T_k = 2^{k-2} + 2(-1)^k$, that is, $T_k = 2^{k-2}/3 + 2(-1)^k/3$.
nodes.title: Number of arch tops in a row of the Calkin–Wilf tree

nodes.summary: Let $L_k$ be the number of P-positions of Euclid in row $k$ of the Calkin–Wilf tree. Then $L_0 = 1$, $L_1 = 0$, $L_{k+2} = L_{k+1} + 2L_k$ for every $k$, and $3L_k = 2^k + 2(-1)^k$ for every $k$, that is, $L_k = 2^k/3 + 2(-1)^k/3$.
nodes.title: Number of P-positions of Euclid in a row of the Calkin–Wilf tree

nodes.summary: For every $k \ge 0$, the number of positions in row $k$ of the Calkin–Wilf tree whose Smith remoteness in the Euclid game is $k$ equals $2^{k/2}$ if $k$ is even and $2^{(k+1)/2}$ if $k$ is odd.
nodes.title: Positions of a Calkin–Wilf row with maximal optimal play in Euclid

nodes.summary: Euclid as an impartial game: its positions are the pairs $(a, b)$ of natural numbers, its moves from $(a, b)$ are the Euclid moves, the rank of $(a, b)$ is $a + b$, and its starting position is $(1, 1)$.
nodes.title: The game Euclid

nodes.summary: If $(a', b')$ is a Euclid move from $(a, b)$, then $a' + b' < a + b$.
nodes.title: Euclid moves lower the sum

nodes.summary: The moves of Euclid from a pair $(a, b)$ of natural numbers are as follows. If $a = b$, $a = 0$ or $b = 0$, there are none. If $0 < a < b$, the moves are to the pairs $(a, b - ja)$ for every integer $j \ge 1$ with $ja < b$; if $0 < b < a$, the moves are to the pairs $(a - jb, b)$ for every integer $j \ge 1$ with $jb < a$.
nodes.title: Euclid moves

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $f$, $a$ and $b$ with $a + b \le f$, the fuel-bounded evaluation of the P-positions of Euclid with fuel $f$ returns true at $(a, b)$ if and only if $(a, b)$ is a normal-play P-position of the Euclid game.

nodes.summary: The fuel-bounded evaluation of the P-positions of Euclid is the function $E(f, a, b)$ of natural numbers $f, a, b$ with Boolean values defined by recursion on the fuel $f$. With no fuel, $E(0, a, b)$ is true. nodes.title: Fuel-bounded Euclid classifier

Let $x, y$ be positive integers. If the daughter $(x+y)/y$ of $x/y$ is a P-position, then so is its niece $(2x+y)/(x+y)$, the daughter of its sibling $x/(x+y)$. nodes.title: Self-similarity of the P-positions of Euclid

nodes.summary: The Euclid P-position test returns true at the pairs $(1, 1)$ and $(3, 2)$ and false at the pairs $(2, 1)$ and $(1, 2)$.
nodes.title: Small P-positions of Euclid

nodes.summary: Call a pair $(a, b)$ of natural numbers a P-position when the Euclid P-position test returns true at $(a, b)$, and read it as the vertex $a/b$ of the Calkin–Wilf tree, with son $a/(a+b)$ and daughter $(a+b)/b$. Let $m, n$ be positive integers. If $m/n$ is a P-position, then so are its son's daughter $(2m+n)/(m+n)$ and its daughter's son $(m+n)/(m+2n)$.
nodes.title: Distinguishing the tops of arches

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $a$ and $b$, the Euclid P-position test at $(a, b)$ is the value at $(a, b)$ of the fuel-bounded evaluation of the P-positions of Euclid with fuel $a + b$.

nodes.title: Fibonacci arch tops

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be the golden ratio. If the pair $(m, n)$, read as the fraction $m/n$, lies in row $k$ of the Calkin–Wilf tree, $m < n$, the position $(m, n)$ of Euclid is not a P-position, and its Smith remoteness in Euclid equals $k$, then $1/(\varphi + 1) < m/n < 1/\varphi$.
nodes.title: Golden-ratio bounds for N-positions of maximal remoteness below 1

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be the golden ratio. If the pair $(m, n)$, read as the fraction $m/n$, lies in row $k$ of the Calkin–Wilf tree, $n < m$, the position $(m, n)$ of Euclid is not a P-position, and its Smith remoteness in Euclid equals $k$, then $\varphi < m/n < \varphi + 1$.
nodes.title: Golden-ratio bounds for N-positions of maximal remoteness above 1

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be the golden ratio. If the pair $(m, n)$, read as the fraction $m/n$, lies in row $k$ of the Calkin–Wilf tree, $m \ne n$, the position $(m, n)$ of Euclid is a P-position, and its Smith remoteness in Euclid equals $k$, then $(\varphi + 2)/(\varphi + 1) < m/n < \varphi$ or $1/\varphi < m/n < (\varphi + 1)/(\varphi + 2)$.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
